items.title: U.S. Industrials and E&C: Data-Center Tailwinds
items.summary: Second-quarter results largely aligned with expectations, as data center-related growth led the way and evidence of broadening short-cycle recovery continued to build. We think these trends remain supportive of ongoing growth momentum, though inflationary pressures remain a challenge.

items.title: North America Transportation: Second-Quarter Earnings Wrap
items.summary: Transports reported strong second-quarter results and signs of an earnings ramp that's expected to extend at least to 2028. But despite beat-and-raise results, stock-price reactions have been decidedly more mixed, largely due to investors' elevated expectations ahead of earnings season.

items.title: Gas Biweekly: How Will E&Ps React to a Bearish 2027?
items.summary: Our forecast for a weaker, oversupplied natural gas market through 2027 poses a question for gas E&Ps: Reduce supply to aid the market balance but risk helping marginal producers and needing to ramp into 2028, or maintain production but risk delaying recovery?

items.title: Global Theme Machine: Momentum Drives the Reshuffle
items.summary: The Theme Model delivered a positive return for July, with the top quintile returning 3.2% against the bottom quintile's 0.5%. Top performers were led by Software as a Service (+10.6%), IT Services (+9.5%), and HR Tech (+9.2%). We dig into the numbers in more detail in this note.

items.title: China Economics: Energy Shock Could Spark New Deflation Risks
items.summary: Deflation risks in China could be rising again following weaker-than-expected July data: Both CPI and PPI missed expectations, driven not only by energy price corrections but also by more pronounced weakness in domestic demand. We look at the potential impacts and possible policy actions.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence: From Buildout to Monetization
items.summary: Despite some political noise around data centers, hyperscaler capex forecasts have increased after second-quarter earnings, with both Google and SpaceX accelerating timelines for infrastructure expansion. Those decisions underscore that the wall of enterprise demand remains vertical.

items.title: Oil Monitor: Hopes for a U.S.-Iran Deal Rise Again
items.summary: Brent eased toward $80 a barrel as markets increasingly focus on a diplomatic answer to U.S.-Iran tensions, with price action suggesting disruption fears are easing more quickly than physical-supply concerns are escalating. But refined product markets still reflect notable tightness.

items.title: Global Macro Strategy: Macro Tapas
items.summary: Our recent "Macro Mezze" note saw us stay bullish on the AI trade and add EMFX carry. With our weekly once again a mix of thematic dishes, we need a new small-plates analogy. We note four questions that keep coming up with clients, offering our answers as well as suggested tactics.

items.title: U.S. Rates Weekly: A Reserve Managers' Treasury Strike?
items.summary: The weak jobs report reinforces our view that the front end of the Treasury curve will remain well anchored; we offer further analysis in this note. We also consider the risk of a reserve manager "buyers' strike" after Treasury’s yen intervention.

items.title: U.S. Economics Weekly: No Reason to Hike
items.summary: A weak July jobs report brought average job growth down to just 20,000 over the last three months and 26,000 over the last 12. Softer job growth should reduce any urgency for a rate hike, but for now the focus remains squarely on inflation, making the upcoming CPI reading a critical one.

items.title: PULSE Monitor: Bad News Is Good, for Now!
items.summary: Data have reminded us of the negative correlation between stocks and economic data, with the NFP report supporting our view that the broadening playbook needs the market to price out Fed hike risk. We look at how that may unfold; despite some asterisks, fundamental tailwinds are at work.

items.title: Global Equity Strategy: The Case for Continued Broadening
items.summary: The building blocks for broader market leadership are emerging: improving cyclical conditions, stronger economic surprises, broader earnings upgrades, and a pause in narrow Tech/AI leadership. We see broadening as expanded market participation, not a rotation away from Tech/AI.

items.title: U.S. Airlines: Supermajors Best Positioned to Outperform
items.summary: We're updating EPS estimates, price targets, and views following earnings season. Fundamentals have improved since the fuel shock, but mixed trends create a complex backdrop. We favor supermajors and reiterate bullish views on DAL, UAL, and AAL, while downgrading JBLU to Sell/High Risk.

items.title: Datadog's C2Q26 Results Reinforce Our Buy Rating
items.summary: DDOG posted strong results, with demand from AI-native and traditional customers validating surging observability needs. Slower growth in contracted revenue and a big customer's usage reduction raise concerns, but conservative guidance and strong execution support sustained mid-30% growth.

items.title: Japan Economics: Regime Shift in BoJ Policy
items.summary: We believe coordinated U.S.-Japan currency intervention marks a turning point, leading us to adopt a more aggressive BoJ outlook. We now expect rate hikes to begin in September and continue through next year, with the policy rate reaching 2%, though the risk of faster hikes remains.

items.title: Mexico Economics: Banxico Reinforcing Stable Rates
items.summary: Banxico kept rates at 6.50% and maintained guidance. A slightly more hawkish inflation outlook reinforces a preference to hold rates steady, not signal hikes. We expect rates to remain at 6.50% through 2027, with persistent services inflation and the Mexico-U.S. rate gap limiting easing.

items.title: U.S. Dollar Monitor: Welcome to Our Inaugural Edition
items.summary: Welcome to the U.S. Dollar Monitor, our overview of the international role of the USD. On a quarterly basis, we'll assess the dollar's performance as measured by real effective exchange rates against both developed and emerging-markets currencies, as well as key bilateral exchange rates.

items.title: World Radar Screen: August Update
items.summary: Emerging markets materially outperformed developed ones across our regional Value/Momentum strategies in July. The market-neutral MSCI AC World portfolio returned 6.1%, notably ahead of the MSCI World strategy at 0.8%. We look at regional performance and what drove EM's strengths herein.

items.title: U.S. Equity Strategy: Recommended List Updates
items.summary: We're updating our U.S. Large Cap Recommended List as well as our Value Creators U.S. SMID Recommended List. For the former, we're adding AS, PAYX and EW, which replace WMT, ROK and MDT. For the latter, we add TOL, DKS, NXT, ESTC and SEI, which replace PAG, BJ, AES, PEGA, CAI and OVV.

items.title: Global Gas and Power Insights: The Super El Niño Effect
items.summary: The potential for a Super El Niño event this winter has heightened investor concerns about extreme cold spells and an associated surge in gas demand. We look at winter weather patterns during three previous strong El Niño episodes to find insights about what could be coming.

items.title: Inside the FDIC's Effort to Modernize Its Frameworks
items.summary: The FDIC is quietly undertaking a comprehensive and significant modernization of its regulatory and supervisory frameworks, an effort aimed at enhancing the resilience and efficiency of the U.S. banking system. We look at the FDIC's three core objectives and potential impacts in this note.

items.title: SpaceEx's Quarter Is a Strong Start to a Multi-Year Arc
items.summary: SpaceEx's results beat expectations, with results at each of its three main segments exceeding our forecasts on all key measures. We’ve described the next two to three years as particularly catalyst-rich; management offered new insight into those catalysts while introducing some new ones.

items.title: We're Downgrading Burlington Stores to Neutral
items.summary: We're downgrading Burlington Stores to Neutral as it's within 5% of our target price and risk/reward no longer skews to the upside. We continue to see BURL and other off-pricers as well positioned to take share, but prefer to move to the sidelines with BURL's stock at all-time highs.

items.title: Three Key Takeaways From Booking Holdings' Results
items.summary: BKNG’s better-than-expected earnings left us incrementally positive, and we highlight key second-quarter takeaways: Travel demand is proving resilient, AI clearly remains a key focus, and Genius and Connected Trip are improving usage and brand loyalty. We raise our target price to $236.

items.title: Arista Beats Results, Shows Confidence in Growth Outlook
items.summary: Arista Networks saw better component supply amid high demand drive upside to results and a 10% increase in the FY26 sales outlook. Buy-rated ANET's targets for AI sales and Campus are unchanged, but management's updated growth outlook includes confidence that those numbers will go higher.

items.title: Caterpillar Keeps Firing on All Cylinders
items.summary: Following Caterpillar's strong second-quarter results, we're raising our 2026 adjusted EPS to $27.05, layering in a ~$2 beat to our estimate in the second quarter along with slightly more constructive second-half top-line assumptions. We're also raising adjusted EPS for 2027 and 2028.

items.title: Shopify's Growth Reaccelerates to a New Cycle High
items.summary: Shopify delivered an exceptional beat in its second quarter, with third-quarter guidance for revenue and free cash flow implying equally strong revisions. With SHOP having underperformed over the last six months, we expect a strong reaction to the beat and reacceleration.

items.title: Emerson Electric Still Looks Poised for Good Upside Over Time
items.summary: Given solid overall results and what we think is good visibility to accelerating growth, we continue to see Emerson Electric as representing favorable risk/reward for longer-term investors. We view  profitability and operating leverage as positive despite unchanged FY26 margin guidance.

items.title: Mexico Diversified Banks: We're Upgrading Regional to Buy
items.summary: Mexican banks are demonstrating earnings resilience in a lukewarm economy, though upward estimate revisions aren't materializing. We're upgrading Regional to Buy, as we see the recent correction and reset in guidance as an attractive opportunity, and offer further analysis herein.

items.title: Global Inflation Monitor: Risks Remain Two-Sided
items.summary: Global headline inflation fell to 2.7% in June from above 3%, but remains more than a half percentage point above its pre-conflict level. All told, risks remain two-sided, depending heavily on the path of oil prices through year's end and the risks of further Middle East disruption.

items.title: Benign Underlying Inflation Could Push Out India's Rate Hikes
items.summary: India once again kept rates unchanged while marginally raising forecasts for growth and lowering ones for inflation. In a dovish move, policymakers lowered their average FY27 core inflation forecast to 4.3% from 4.7%. Given these numbers, we don't foresee a rate hike in 2026.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence: Capex + Time = Profits
items.summary: Hyperscaler cloud revenue accelerated to +48% in the second quarter from +39% in the first amid a continued acceleration in enterprise adoption. But consensus continues to underestimate future revenue growth and profitability tied to AI. The math is simple: capex + time = profits.

items.title: Food for Thought: How Are EVs Impacting Brazil's Fuels Demand?
items.summary: The rapid acceleration of EV sales in Brazil raises an increasingly pressing question for the fuels sector: When does this shift begin to structurally and visibly erode Otto Cycle fuels demand? Our answer is that the impact, while modest in aggregate terms, is already real and rising.

items.title: AI Chipmakers to Pivot from Scale-Up to Scale-Out
items.summary: Amid persistent memory shortages, we expect AI chipmakers to increasingly scale out by deploying more GPUs with lower HBM content. We also expect HBM supply to remain tight, as memory suppliers stay disciplined in expanding output amid attractive server economics.

items.title: Metal Matters: Exploring Our Base Case for Gold
items.summary: In our base case, gold prices stagnate or even decline over the next month before rallying to $4,500 an ounce in the fourth quarter and to $5,000 by next year's first half. In this note we look at the reasons for gold's sell-off and what we see shaping prices in the months ahead.

items.title: We're Initiating Coverage of Brunello Cucinelli at Buy
items.summary: We're initiating coverage of Brunello Cucinelli with a Buy rating and a €110 target price. As explored herein, we believe BCU's competitive advantages can endure longer than the market discounts and think current brand-related concerns are overdone, offering an attractive entry point.

items.title: Agnico Eagle Mines' Track Record Keeps Us Constructive
items.summary: We've heard investor worries that Agnico might be starting to overextend, with multiple potential projects on deck and Finland now added to the mix. It's a fair question, but AEM has a long track record running arguably the best gold miner in the world, and so we stick with our Buy rating.

items.title: Equity Markets Positioning Model: Rebuild Continues for Europe
items.summary: Positioning continues to move further out of sync with index performance. Europe stands out as the only major region experiencing a meaningful improvement in risk appetite, supported by fresh long accumulation and favorable earnings delivery. We also offer analysis for the U.S. and Asia.

items.title: Global FX Strategy: What's Next for JPY?
items.summary: The intervention-driven JPY rally may be reaching its limit for now. Ultimately, we see interventions alone as insufficient to turn the JPY tide. That will require a more aggressive policy from the Bank of Japan and/or relief on the fiscal front. We offer further analysis herein.

items.title: Africa Weekly: The Outlook for the Eco and the Ghana Cedi
items.summary: We consider the implications of the recent announcement by the regional union ECOWAS to move ahead with the introduction of its proposed Eco currency. We also explore evolving changes in the system for auctioning foreign exchange in Ghana and how they might affect the value of the cedi.
